title: 2015年考研英语一 Part B · 七选五

sentences: Directions: In the following text, some sentences have been removed.
For Questions 41-45, choose the most suitable one from the list A-G to fit into each of the numbered blanks.
There are two extra choices, which do not fit in any of the blanks.
Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET.
(10 points)
translations: 说明：在下面的文本中，有一些句子已被删除。
对于问题41-45，从列表A-G中选择最合适的一个填入每个编号的空白处。
有两个额外的选项，它们不适合任何空白处。
在答题卡上标记你的答案。

sentences: How does your reading proceed?
Clearly you try to comprehend, in the sense of identifying meanings for individual words and working out relationships between them, drawing on your implicit knowledge of English grammar.
translations: 你的阅读如何进行？
显然，你试图理解，即识别单个单词的含义并理清它们之间的关系，利用你对英语语法的隐性知识。

sentences: You begin to infer a context for the text, for instance, by making decisions about what kind of speech event is involved: Who is making the utterance, to whom, when and where.
translations: 你开始推断文本的语境，例如，通过决定涉及什么样的言语事件：谁在说话，对谁，何时何地。

sentences: The ways of reading indicated here are without doubt kinds of comprehension.
But they show comprehension to consist not just of passive assimilation but of active engagement in inference and problem-solving.
You infer information you feel the writer has invited you to grasp by presenting you with specific evidence and clues.
translations: 这里指出的阅读方式无疑是理解的各种形式。
但它们表明理解不仅包括被动吸收，还包括主动参与推理和解决问题。
你推断出你认为作者通过提供具体证据和线索邀请你掌握的信息。

sentences: Conceived in this way, comprehension will not follow exactly the same track for each reader.
What is in question is not the retrieval of an absolute, fixed or “true” meaning that can be read off and checked for accuracy, or some timeless relation of the text to the world.
translations: 以这种方式构想，理解不会对每个读者遵循完全相同的轨迹。
问题不在于检索一个绝对的、固定的或“真实的”意义，可以读取并检查准确性，或文本与世界的某种永恒关系。

sentences: Such background material inevitably reflects who we are.
translations: 这样的背景材料不可避免地反映了我们是谁。

sentences: This doesn’t, however, make interpretation merely relative or even pointless.

Precisely because readers from different historical periods, places and social experiences produce different but overlapping readings of the same words on the page—including for texts that engage with fundamental human concerns—debates about texts can play an important role in social discussion of beliefs and values.
translations: 然而，这并不使解释仅仅是相对的，甚至毫无意义。
正是因为来自不同历史时期、地点和社会经验的读者对页面上的相同文字产生不同但重叠的解读——包括涉及人类基本关切的文本——关于文本的辩论可以在信仰和价值观的社会讨论中发挥重要作用。

sentences: How we read a given text also depends to some extent on our particular interest in reading it.
Such dimensions of reading suggest—as others introduced later in the book will also do—that we bring an implicit (often unacknowledged) agenda to any act of reading.
It doesn’t then necessarily follow that one kind of reading is fuller, more advanced or more worthwhile than another.
Ideally, different kinds of reading inform each other, and act as useful reference points for and counterbalances to one another.
Together, they make up the reading component of your overall literacy, or relationship to your surrounding textual environment.
translations: 我们如何阅读一个给定的文本也在某种程度上取决于我们对阅读它的特定兴趣。
阅读的这些维度表明——正如本书后面介绍的其他维度也会表明的那样——我们为任何阅读行为带来一个隐含的（通常未被承认的）议程。
这并不一定意味着一种阅读比另一种更完整、更先进或更有价值。
理想情况下，不同的阅读方式相互启发，并作为彼此有用的参考点和平衡。
它们共同构成了你整体素养的阅读组成部分，或与你周围文本环境的关系。

sentences: [A] Are we studying that text and trying to respond in a way that fulfils the requirement of a given course?
Reading it simply for pleasure?
Skimming it for information?
Ways of reading on a train or in bed are likely to differ considerably from reading in a seminar room.
translations: [A] 我们是在研究那个文本并试图以符合给定课程要求的方式回应吗？
仅仅为了消遣而阅读它？
为了获取信息而略读它？
在火车上或床上阅读的方式很可能与在研讨室阅读大不相同。

sentences: [B] Factors such as the place and period in which we are reading, our gender, ethnicity, age and social class will encourage us towards certain interpretations but at the same time obscure or even close off others.
translations: [B] 诸如我们阅读的地点和时期、我们的性别、民族、年龄和社会阶层等因素将鼓励我们走向某些解释，但同时模糊甚至封闭其他解释。

sentences: [C] If you are unfamiliar with words or idioms, you guess at their meaning, using clues presented in the context.
On the assumption that they will become relevant later, you make a mental note of discourse entities as well as possible links between them.
translations: [C] 如果你不熟悉单词或习语，你根据语境中提供的线索猜测它们的含义。
假设它们以后会变得相关，你会在心里记下话语实体以及它们之间可能的联系。

sentences: [D] In effect, you try to reconstruct the likely meanings or effects that any given sentence, image or reference might have had: These might be the ones the author intended.
translations: [D] 实际上，你试图重建任何给定句子、图像或引用可能具有的可能含义或效果：这些可能是作者意图的。

sentences: [E] You make further inferences, for instance, about how the text may be significant to you, or about its validity—inferences that form the basis of a personal response for which the author will inevitably be far less responsible.
translations: [E] 你做出进一步的推断，例如，关于文本可能对你有多重要，或关于其有效性——这些推断构成了个人回应的基础，而作者对此必然远不那么负责。

sentences: [F] In plays, novels and narrative poems, characters speak as constructs created by the author, not necessarily as mouthpieces for the author’s own thoughts.
translations: [F] 在戏剧、小说和叙事诗中，人物作为作者创造的构造物说话，不一定是作者自己思想的喉舌。

sentences: [G] Rather, we ascribe meanings to texts on the basis of interaction between what we might call textual and contextual material: between kinds of organization or patterning we perceive in a text’s formal structures (so especially its language structures) and various kinds of background, social knowledge, belief and attitude that we bring to the text.
translations: [G] 相反，我们根据我们可能称之为文本和语境材料之间的相互作用来赋予文本意义：在我们感知到的文本形式结构（尤其是其语言结构）中的组织或模式类型与我们带给文本的各种背景、社会知识、信仰和态度之间。
